dē-sūmo , mpsi (msi), 3, v. a. Lit.,
I.to take for one's self from a multitude or mass; hence, to pick out, choose, select (syn. deligere); to take upon one's self, undertake (rare, and perh. not ante-Aug.— “syn. suscipere): sibi consules asservandos desumunt,” Liv. 4, 55, 3 : “sibi hostes,” id. 38, 45 ; cf.: “sibi pugnas,” Tac. Or. 37 ; and: “cursum certamenque,” Plin. Ep. 8, 20, 7 : sibi vacuas Athenas, *Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 81.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
